data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'nakshatra', meaning 'star'. In Hindu astrology, each of the 27 constellations is associated with a 'nakshatra'. The name Naksh signifies the cosmic influence of the stars and the divine power of the universe. The name Naksh carries the meaning “Sky, star, or mark” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Naksh usually hope their child will grow to embody sky, star, or mark and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The name 'Naksh' is mentioned in the epics of Mahabharata and Ramayana in reference to the constellation of Ursa Major, also known as the Great Bear. This constellation was considered sacred in Hindu astronomy and astrology, and was believed to be home to various deities, including Indra and the Seven Rishis.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata and Ramayana are ancient Indian texts that form part of the Hindu scriptures. They contain mythological narratives, philosophical discourses, and historical and geographical references.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the name 'Naksh' can be found in the Puranic texts, particularly the Vayu Purana. In this text, 'Naksh' is mentioned as a divine being who is the son of the goddess Aditi and the god Prajapati. He is considered to be the god of the north, and is often depicted riding a chariot pulled by white horses.
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a set of eighteen major Sanskrit texts in Hinduism that discuss various aspects of Hindu mythology, philosophy, and history. They are believed to have been composed between the 6th and 12th centuries CE.
